newsitem.title: USA: Musicland sees higher Q2 EBITDA.
newsitem.headline: Musicland sees higher Q2 EBITDA.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said Thursday it expects earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) for the second quarter to be better than a year-ago.

"Despite soft sales in June and the second quarter, we expect second quarter EBITDA results to be ahead of last year and ahead of plan, due largely to higher margins and reduced expenses," Reid Johnson, chief financial officer, said in a statement.

Howevever, Johnson added that trade vendor support in the form of normal credit terms will be required to allow the company to have a successful holiday season and achieve long-term financial plans and viability.
In the year-ago second quarter, Musicland had an operating loss of $9.2 million before depreciation, amortization and a restructuring charge.
Earlier, Musicland reported a 1.8 percent rise in comparable-store sales for the five weeks ended July 5.
With fewer stores, total sales for the five-week period declined as expected by 5.1 percent to $137.3 million compared with $144.6 million for the year-ago five week period, Musicland said.

Comparable-store sales for the Mall Stores Division (Sam Goody/Musicland and Suncoast Motion Picture Co) increased 3.8 percent. Total division sales for June declined 0.7 percent to $90.6 million versus $91.3 million a year ago, since the company operated six percent fewer mall stores.
Comparable-store sales for the Superstores Division (Media Play and On Cue) decreased by 2.2 percent versus a more promotional June last year when sales were up 7.8 percent.

Total sales for the Superstores Division declined by 12.4 percent to $45.7 million compared with $52.2 million in June 1996. On June 30, the company operated 19 percent fewer Media Play stores than the prior year, while the number of On Cue stores remained about the same.
For the 26 weeks ended July 5, Musicland's comparable-store sales were nearly flat, compared with a decline of 1.3 percent last year.
